record.paper_title: PROGRESS IN THE OPEN PROBLEMS IN THEORY OF FUNCTIONS OF BOUNDED INDEX
record.context_brief: Bounded directional index for PDE solutions
record.original_question: Let L: C^n → R_+ be a positive continuous function, and for a nonzero direction b ∈ C^n define the directional derivatives by ∂F/∂b = Σ_{j=1}^n b_j ∂F/∂z_j and ∂^kF/∂b^k by iterating this operator. An entire function F on C^n is said to have bounded L-index in the direction b if there exists m_0 such that for every m and every z, the normalized derivative (1/(m! L(z)^m))|∂^mF(z)/∂b^m| is bounded above by the maximum of the same normalized quantities for orders 0 through m_0. Suppose P_1(z_1,z_2) and P_2(z_1,z_2) are entire functions of bounded L-index in the coordinate directions e_1=(1,0) and e_2=(0,1), respectively. For which directions b, and under what additional assumptions, must every entire solution F of the first-order partial differential equation P_1(z_1,z_2) ∂F/∂z_1 + P_2(z_1,z_2) ∂F/∂z_2 = h(z_1,z_2) also have bounded L-index in the direction b?

evidence.quote: An entire function F(z), z ∈ C^n, is called ([11, 12]) a function of bounded L-index in a direction b = (b1, . . . , bn) ∈ C^n \ {0}, if there exists m0 ∈ Z+ such that for every m ∈ Z+ and every z ∈ C^n ...
Let us consider the following partial differential equation P1(z1, z2) ∂F/∂z1 + P2(z1, z2) ∂F/∂z2 = h(z1, z2). (1)

Problem 1 ([10, Problem 3]). Let P1(z1, z2), P2(z1, z2) be entire functions of bounded L-index in directions e1 = (1, 0) and e2 = (0, 1) respectively. What are a direction b and additional assumptions such that every entire solution F(z) of equation (1) has a bounded L-index in the direction b?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{R}_+$ be a positive continuous function. For a nonzero direction $\mathbf{b}=(b_1,\dots,b_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$, define the directional derivative $\partial_{\mathbf{b}} F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial F(z)/\partial z_j$, and define $\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^k F$ by iterating this operator. The function $F$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$ if there exists $m_0\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that
$$\frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^m F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\le \max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|\partial_{\mathbf{b}}^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k}\qquad\text{for all }m\in\mathbb{Z}_+\text{ and all }z\in\mathbb{C}^n.$$
Now consider the case $n=2$ with coordinate directions $\mathbf{e}_1=(1,0)$ and $\mathbf{e}_2=(0,1)$. Let $P_1,P_2:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be entire functions such that $P_1$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $P_2$ has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{e}_2$, and let $h:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ be entire. Determine the directions $\mathbf{b}\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ and additional assumptions on $P_1,P_2,h,L$ under which every entire solution $F$ of the first-order partial differential equation
$$P_1(z_1,z_2)\,\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_1}+P_2(z_1,z_2)\,\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_2}=h(z_1,z_2)$$
necessarily has bounded $L$-index in the direction $\mathbf{b}$.
artifact.category_tag: Entire functions of bounded L-index in direction
artifact.status_search_result: Surveys on progress in problems on functions of bounded index list this as an open problem regarding first-order linear PDEs in two complex variables. Related results exist for second-order equations (Bandura–Skaskiv, Acta Comm. Univ. Tartu. Math., 2018) and linear PDEs in general, but a complete characterization of admissible directions and additional hypotheses for the stated first-order equation does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of the L-index in a direction of entire solutions of second order partial differential equation
status_evidence.snippet: Treats second-order PDEs; the first-order analogue with general P1,P2 of bounded directional L-index remains a posed problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses second-order equations, while the first-order problem remains stated as open in surveys on progress in bounded-index theory.

status_evidence.title: Properties of entire solutions of some linear PDE's
status_evidence.snippet: Studies bounded L-index properties of entire solutions to linear PDEs.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results in the program but does not resolve the first-order two-variable problem in full generality.
